purpose: Primaquine is used to treat and prevent certain types of malaria, particularly a type called vivax malaria. It works by killing the malaria parasite that hides in your liver, which helps prevent the infection from coming back. It is often used after another malaria medicine to make sure the infection is completely cleared from your body.
how_it_works: Malaria parasites can hide in your liver and come back later to make you sick again. Primaquine works by targeting and destroying these hidden parasites in the liver before they can re-enter your bloodstream. Think of it like a cleanup crew that sweeps out the last hiding parasites so the infection does not return.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, and loss of appetite are the most common side effects. Taking the medicine with food can help reduce stomach discomfort. You may also notice some mild headache or dizziness.
warnings: This medicine can cause a serious condition called hemolytic anemia in people who have a genetic condition called G6PD deficiency, where red blood cells break down too quickly. Your doctor must test you for G6PD deficiency before you start this medicine. It should NOT be used during pregnancy. Tell your doctor about all your medicines and health conditions before taking primaquine.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 15 to 30 mg once daily for 14 days, taken by mouth with food. Your doctor will decide the exact dose and length of treatment based on the type of malaria and your health. Always finish the full course even if you feel better.
